gui.createcheme.equipment_constructor.ce: Impeller diameter, 0.3 to 1.5 m in 0.1 m steps; the casing (1.9 times as wide), bearings, nozzles, gear, motor, table and lube-oil console follow. The flow grows with its square
Impellers in the casing, 2 to 9; each lengthens the casing by 0.35 of the impeller diameter and adds head and shaft power, so the gear and motor grow with them
Height of the operating deck on the concrete table, 4 to 7 m in whole metres; at least 4 m, 5 m from a 0.5 m impeller and 6 m from 0.8 m, so the suction line's elbow and strainer fit under the slab
Inlet flow and shaft power scaled from a 0.65 m, four-impeller Elliott 32M4 (33,000 m³/h, 2.5 MW) with the impeller's area and the impellers; the speed keeps the impeller tips at 245 m/s
gui.createcheme.equipment_constructor.cy: Cyclone body diameter, 0.3 to 2 m in 0.1 m steps; Stairmand's high-efficiency proportions set the inlet, gas outlet, cylinder (1.5 diameters) and cone (2.5). From 1.2 m a roof walkway with a caged ladder
Cyclones in parallel, 1 to 4, a diameter and 1.5 m apart on common inlet and outlet headers; several drop their dust through their airlocks into one screw conveyor

Height of the cone's dust outlet flange above the ground, up to 8 m in whole metres; at least as high as hang the dipleg or hopper, the airlock and the conveyor, with the solids outlet a block over the ground
Air through all the cyclones at 20 m/s in their inlets; the cut size is the mineral dust (2.5 g/cm³) caught half the time (Lapple). Smaller cyclones catch finer dust
